# the canon shows the surviving `**` -- so the layered-defaults ladder
# (***org / **env / *tenant) keeps its arbitration and the default
# stays overridable after the kind meet. Canon rows because gen cannot
# see the preference.
# A PREFERENCE CONJOINED WITH A DISJUNCTION IS A PREFERENCE ON THE

# direct spelling denotes. Distribution carries the peer to each
# member, and the kind gate then replaces a scalar preference BY the
# concrete member it met -- so the preference simply vanished, and the
# enum-with-default written this way round held no default at all. The
# old generation fold hid it; ADR-007 does not. A preference naming no
# alternative is dropped: it has nothing to prefer, and the
# default-validity lint is what reports that shape.

# THE KIND GATE MUST SURVIVE A CLONE.
# A preference is a default, so a concrete peer replaces it -- but only
# where the peer is the same KIND of thing (`*1 & 2` is 2; `*1 & {}` is an
# error). The gate is the preferred value's own `superpeg`. It once widened
# to the numeric FAMILY, which also let `*8080 & 3.5` through; see
# test/spec/number-tower.tsv for the rows that pin the narrower rule.
# Uncloned, both ports already refused: `x:*1&{}` errors in both. Every row
# below reaches the PrefVal through a clone -- a spread template, a $ref, a
# copy() -- which is where Go dropped the gate entirely and accepted a map,
# a string, a boolean or a list as an override. Not weakened: absent.
# The last two rows are the ones that must NOT move. A gate that rejects
# everything would pass all the error rows above and break the language.
pref-kind-gate-spread-map-err
pref-kind-gate-spread-string-err
pref-kind-gate-spread-bool-err
pref-kind-gate-spread-list-err
pref-kind-gate-ref-clone-err

# THE GATE IS super(), SO A STRUCTURAL DEFAULT HAS ONE AT LAST.
# These rows used to record the opposite: a map or a list inherited
# FeatureVal.superior(), which is TOP, so `unite(top, peer)` was the
# peer and ANY value overrode a structural default -- including one of
# another kind entirely, and a map that merely added a key REPLACED
# the default rather than merging with it.
# They were recorded "so that change cannot be made by accident, in
# one port only, or without noticing which of the two behaviours
# moved". ADR-011 is that change, made on purpose, in both ports.
# `super({x:1})` is `{x:integer}`, and the meet asks the two questions
# the long form asks: does the preferred value ITSELF admit the peer
# (maps merge, so `x` survives), and if not does its type? A string
# answers neither, so nothing of the default remains -- `empty`.
# The replace-anything reading stays spellable, as `*{x:1} | top`.
pref-struct-map-default-refuses-string
pref-struct-list-default-refuses-string
pref-struct-map-default-merges
pref-struct-list-default-refuses-number
# The scalar direction of the same pairing, for contrast: a scalar
# default refuses a map, and says so as the emptied disjunction it is

# inner meet rather than of anything the author wrote).
pref-scalar-default-refuses-map
pref-override-ref-clone-gens
# THE ADMISSION GATE (ADR-004, 2026-08-26). A peer that meets a scalar
# preference INSIDE a disjunction must be admitted by the disjunction:
# by some sibling alternative, or by the preferred value itself. The
# old rule let the pref's kind gate alone decide, so a same-kind
# concrete peer replaced the default with the alternatives never
# consulted -- `k:*'auto'|'literal'|'data'` + `k:'autoo'` answered
# "autoo" with exit 0 (use-cases/BUGS.md §1), and a constraint branch
# that EXCLUDED the override (`*8080|(integer&neq(80))` + 80) was
# bypassed (§2). `*A|B|C` is now the enum-with-default every consumer
# already believed it was: unset generates A, members override, a
# non-member is the `empty` refusal. The deliberately-open default
# keeps its spelling: `*x|top` admits every override (the apidef
# machine-emitted `*(x)|top` idiom). Structural and kind-peg defaults
# stay ungated (the scalar-gate boundary above). All rows parity-probed.
pref-admit-enum-nonmember-refused
pref-admit-enum-member-overrides
pref-admit-enum-default
pref-admit-constraint-branch-refuses
pref-admit-constraint-branch-admits
pref-admit-constraint-branch-default
pref-admit-neq-branch-refuses

# A PREFERENCE MARKS A VALUE, AND A BARE KEY IS NOT ONE.
# `*a: 1` has no braces, so the `*` took the whole IMPLICIT top-level
# map as its operand and the document silently became `*{"a":1}`. With
# a second entry it was worse: `*a: 1, b: 2` parsed as the one-element
# LIST `[*{"a":1}]`, losing `b` outright. Neither is anything the author
# wrote, and the accident was confined to the first position of the
# implicit top-level map -- the only place where no brace has yet
# committed the rule to a map. `{*a: 1}` and `a: 1, *b: 2` were already
# parse errors; these rows make the third spelling agree with them.
# Every expectation was obtained by running BOTH engines and diffing.
pref-implicit-bag-refused
pref-implicit-bag-refused-two

# map alternative needs. Pinned here so the guard above cannot widen.
# They keep their WRITTEN shape under ADR-011 too (R6): a container
# default is leafwise in what it ADMITS, not in how it is spelled.
